findings.contract: .agent/packets/GL3-AUDIT-A5B.md requires identical canonical filter scope for bounded group traversal and client group members, with no filtered-out records shown as current; page-transition packet requires current rows and action targets to match the requested cohort.
findings.trigger: Start expanding a partial multi-record group and delay its scoped group-page response. Change an authoritative member filter such as activity or geography so the new list retains the same stable group ID but only one eligible member; let the new list response commit, then release the old group response.
findings.evidence: toggleGroup captures tier/search/decision/filters/token at invocation and awaits one or more group-page requests. It does not check the current page key, navigation epoch, token, or latest expansion intent before unconditionally writing expandedGroupMembers[card.key] and expandedCardKey. The filter handler clears the map, and the new list request also clears it, but an older group request can finish afterward and repopulate that same stable group key. cards then replaces the current server-selected members with the stale array. serverProjectCards retains the stable group ID even when filtered membership changes, and the backend group endpoint applies the old request's own filter scope. The row can consequently display or open a member excluded from the current filter; a late old-scope group error can also appear over a newer current page.
findings.impact: Bounded traversal can cross the client filter authority boundary and expose a record as part of the current filtered group when the current server page excludes it. The 57-pass browser suite covers page transitions but has no delayed group-hydration/scope-switch case.
findings.required_correction: Bind group hydration to the exact current cohort/page token and a request or navigation epoch. Apply members and errors only while that scope and the intended expanded group still match; discard or abort older responses. Keep bounded group paging and add a delayed old-group response after a filter change that preserves group ID but narrows membership, asserting the excluded member is never displayed or openable.

findings.contract: A5B requires each partial group's bounded members to remain independently inspectable under current browse state; latest user navigation must not be overwritten by an earlier pending request.
findings.trigger: Begin expanding partial group A with a delayed group-page response, then expand group B; let B complete before A.
findings.evidence: Both toggleGroup invocations see their own captured card. Each completion unconditionally sets expandedCardKey to its card key at line 496. When A finishes last it reopens A even though B is the user's latest selection. The same unguarded path can set an obsolete error after navigation.
findings.impact: The visible expanded group can switch to the wrong card after a late response, undermining inspection and exact-member selection.
findings.required_correction: Use one latest-expansion intent or epoch shared with scope validation. Ignore an older group's success/error after a newer expansion, collapse, filter, tier, page, or navigation action; add an out-of-order two-group browser case.
